subject.title: feat(skills): add option to disable ~/.agents/skills scanning for Claude Code coexistence

question: Which public contract should OpenClaw expose, if any, for disabling built-in skill source roots such as `agents-skills-personal`?
rationale: The source-level problem is real, but every plausible fix adds public `skills.load` configuration and changes built-in skill-source behavior, which repository policy reserves for maintainer product/API judgment.

options.title: Add typed `disabledSources`
options.body: Expose a narrow enum-like list of built-in skill source ids, default to current behavior, and skip disabled sources before discovery and watcher registration.

options.title: Add a personal-source toggle
options.body: Expose a smaller boolean for `~/.agents/skills` only, reducing API surface but leaving project-agent and future source opt-outs unresolved.

options.title: Keep current loading model
options.body: Decline new config surface and document per-agent skill allowlists, prompt limits, and per-skill disables as the supported controls.

recommendation.title: Add typed `disabledSources`
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow enum-like list of built-in skill source ids, default to current behavior, and skip disabled sources before discovery and watcher registration.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest verified recent history on the skills config, loader, watcher, and docs surfaces that the decision would change.
